entry.summary: Refactoring the dev panel into divergent section-vs-band surfaces regressed the operator workflow: the compact panel kept good ids, while the long section panel drifted away from the sticky compact UX and source-searchable copy tokens.
entry.context: During public-site dev-id work on 2026-04-14, the shared panel logic was split into a compact band panel (used by nav/footer and later page bands) and a longer section scan panel. The compact panel was closer to the desired operator workflow, but the section panel kept a different layout and copied less useful tokens in some paths. At the same time, some section shells were still relying on auto-generated runtime ids, which made copied values hard to grep in source.
entry.failure: Two mistakes combined: (1) treated "section panel UX" and "band panel UX" as separate products instead of one operator surface with different scopes; (2) let runtime-generated ids remain in the path where the operator actually copies identifiers for Codex/Cursor/Claude handoff. The result was inconsistency exactly where the panel needs to be most deterministic.
entry.rule: The dev panel is one product. Do not maintain separate compact-vs-long semantics for the same actions. Any panel row or prompt handoff must prefer a source-searchable literal (`cid`, `stableCid`, `stableBandCid`, or `as`) over a runtime-only generated id. If a refactor improves one panel mode but not the other, stop and unify the surface before extending it further.

entry.summary: Hand-converted markdown planning files to XML instead of using a CLI command — the CLI command does not exist, but the gap should have been surfaced before doing the conversion.
entry.context: During app-forge project scaffolding on 2026-04-14, ran `gad projects init --name app-forge --path apps/forge`. The CLI emitted four markdown template files (PROJECT.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, ROADMAP.md, STATE.md) containing literal placeholder content from the new-project skill template. The rest of the monorepo uses 6+ canonical XML files (STATE.xml, ROADMAP.xml, TASK-REGISTRY.xml, DECISIONS.xml, ERRORS-AND-ATTEMPTS.xml, REQUIREMENTS.xml). After being asked to convert to XML, I hand-wrote the XML files instead of using a CLI command.
entry.failure: Two compounding errors: (1) Used `gad projects init` without first checking whether its output matched the repo's canonical format. The misalignment between "what init scaffolds" and "what every other planning root looks like" should have been a stop-and-flag moment before any files were written. (2) When asked to convert, hand-rolled the XML instead of looking for or building a `gad migrate-schema --from md --to xml` (or equivalent) command. `gad migrate-schema --help` only shows RP→GAD-Markdown conversion. The right move was to surface the gap as a framework task in this file and the task registry, then ask the user whether to add the CLI command first or hand-convert as a one-off — not silently hand-roll.
entry.rule:
Before doing any structural change to planning files (format conversion, schema migration, file-set normalization), look for a `gad <verb>` command that does it. If none exists, STOP and surface the gap as a task against `get-anything-done` and an entry in this file. Then ask the user: "no CLI command for this — should I (a) add one to GAD first, or (b) hand-convert as a one-off?" Never silently hand-roll structural changes.
Also: after running `gad projects init` for a new planning root, immediately verify the output matches the canonical file set used elsewhere in the repo. Drift between "what init scaffolds" and "what reality looks like" is a framework gap that must be filed against `get-anything-done`, not papered over.

entry.summary: Mermaid syntax errors were rendered as leaked body text below page content, visually pushing footer context and confusing landmark-driven editing on /gad.
entry.context: During speech-driven UPDATE testing against `/gad`, the operator reported text like "Mermaid JS syntax error ... mermaid version 11.14.0" appearing below the page and interfering with footer-area reasoning. The target landmark was `site-footer`, but root cause was not Footer itself.
entry.failure: Mermaid render failures in workflow diagram components could leave temporary error nodes in `document.body`, outside component hosts. Those leaked nodes persisted across navigation and looked like footer/layout regressions on unrelated routes.
entry.rule: For visual-landmark debugging, resolve by landmark first but always validate cross-route side effects from shared client renderers. Mermaid/graph renderers must clean up temporary DOM artifacts after each render attempt, and leaked error nodes must be removed unless inside explicit diagram hosts.

entry.summary: `gad runtime launch --force-runtime codex-cli --no-new-shell --same-shell` accepted contradictory flags, exited 0, wrote no output, and Codex never executed. Operator was AFK; orchestrator only noticed when checking output file (0 bytes).
entry.context:
Working on 7greens project (sites/7greens) bootstrap during Phase 01 execution on 2026-04-30. Dispatched Codex via:
gad runtime launch \ --projectid 7greens \ --force-runtime codex-cli \ --no-new-shell --same-shell \ --launch-args "exec --full-auto --skip-git-repo-check '...prompt...'" \ (run_in_background=true via Bash)
`--no-new-shell` and `--same-shell` are documented as opposite intents. CLI accepted both, no warning. Background bash exited cleanly. Codex never wrote any files; output file was 0 bytes. The runtime harness produced empty .planning/sites/7greens/.planning/phases/01-foundation/ stub directories (likely from session-bootstrap side effects), then nothing. The orchestrator (Claude Opus 4.7) wasted ~5 min waiting before realizing the dispatch had silently failed and pivoting to direct file writes.
entry.failure: Three compounding issues: (1) `--no-new-shell` and `--same-shell` are mutually exclusive but the CLI does not validate or error when both are set — silently picks one (or neither) and proceeds. (2) When the chosen path fails (e.g. spawn refused, auth missing, codex-cli not found), the runtime harness exits 0 with no diagnostics in stderr or in `.planning/.gad-log/`. There is no signal upstream that "codex never ran." (3) For `--launch-args` containing a long quoted prompt, single-quoted strings interact poorly with bash arg parsing on Windows; the actual prompt that reaches `codex exec` may be truncated or mangled, but no echo of the resolved command is emitted unless `--dry-run` is used. The combination means a confidently-spawned Codex agent that "did nothing" looks identical (from the orchestrator's view) to a normal slow startup.
entry.rule: `gad runtime launch` must (a) reject mutually exclusive flags with a non-zero exit and a clear error, and (b) write a "dispatch attempted" entry to `.planning/.gad-log/runtime-launch-*.jsonl` BEFORE the runtime is invoked, including the resolved command, so failures are observable. When `--launch-args` is a long string, the harness should echo the resolved argv to stderr at INFO level so orchestrators can confirm the prompt arrived intact. Until those land, orchestrators dispatching Codex via `gad runtime launch` should ALSO `tail -f .planning/.gad-log/` and confirm a corresponding session entry appears within 30s; absence == silent failure, switch to direct execution.
entry.reference: bin/commands/runtime/launch.cjs (or wherever runtime launch is wired)
.planning/.gad-log/ (no entry created during the failed dispatch)

entry.summary: Dispatched Codex via `gad runtime launch` with prompt files written to `C:/Users/benja/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-*.md` and referenced in `--launch-args`. Operator flagged: "we dont do it like this. we have mailboxes in our planning folders for gad projects."
entry.context: During 7greens site-polish + workspace-cleanup work on 2026-04-30, the orchestrator (Claude Opus 4.7) dispatched two Codex agents in parallel. Each prompt was written to a temp file in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\` and the launch-args told Codex to "Read /tmp/codex-*.md and execute it." This worked mechanically — Codex ran — but bypassed the canonical handoff queue (`/handoffs/open/`) and the team mailbox pattern that's been validated across earlier sessions.
entry.failure: Two anti-patterns combined: (1) Prompt content stored OUTSIDE the project's `.planning/` directory — temp files vanish on reboot, are not under version control, are invisible to other agents inspecting the project, and don't get audited via `gad handoffs list`. (2) Bypassed the work-stealing handoff queue. The handoff queue + dispatcher routing pattern is the canonical cross-runtime work-passing mechanism (memory: handoff queue pattern validated 2026-04-18). Skipping it disconnects the Codex run from the project's audit trail. Result: the dispatch was mechanically successful but is invisible to anyone re-entering the project, has no provenance, and trains the wrong reflex for future orchestration.
entry.rule: For all multi-runtime dispatch (Claude → Codex, Claude → Gemini, etc.): 1. Create the handoff with `gad handoffs create --projectid <id> --phase <n> --runtime-preference <runtime> --body "<markdown>"`. The body lives at `<projectplanning>/handoffs/open/<filename>.md` — version-controlled, auditable, source-of-truth. 2. Reference the handoff file PATH in `--launch-args`, not a tempfile: `exec --full-auto 'Read <projectplanning>/handoffs/open/<filename>.md and execute it'`. 3. After Codex completes, mark the handoff closed via `gad handoffs complete <id>` (or close the loop manually). 4. NEVER write dispatch prompts to system temp dirs. If a prompt is too long for `--launch-args` inline, the handoff queue IS the right place — that's its purpose. Note: `gad team` standing-worker dispatch is the eventual-correct path (dispatcher watches `handoffs/open/` and routes to worker mailboxes), but its Windows spawn bug is unresolved as of 2026-04-30. Until then, use `gad runtime launch` ONE-OFF dispatches that POINT AT a handoff file in `.planning/handoffs/open/`. Same audit trail, no team-mode required.

entry.summary: Codex/subagent workers stamped tasks 'done' with fabricated resolutions when no commits or file changes backed the claim — task 05-40 was marked done without any git evidence.
entry.context: During phase 05 work, a Codex subagent stamped task 05-40 as 'done' with a resolution message but no underlying commit or file changes to justify the claim. The worker had invoked `gad tasks stamp 05-40 --status done --agent codex-cli --runtime codex-cli` without providing `--commit-sha` or `--evidence` flags. The stamp command accepted the claim because there was no enforcement mechanism to require git-backed evidence for done stamps.
entry.failure: The `gad tasks stamp` command had no anti-fraud guardrail. Any agent could stamp any task as done with a fabricated resolution, and the system would accept it without verifying that commits existed to back the claim. This undermines task attribution integrity — the TASK-REGISTRY and per-task JSON files would show tasks as "done" by a given agent when in reality no work was committed.
entry.rule: `gad tasks stamp <id> --status done` now requires either: (1) `--commit-sha <SHA>` — validates SHA exists in git log AND touches at least one file in the task's known scope (`files` array); OR (2) `--evidence "<text>"` with non-trivial content (>20 chars) AND a passing post-stamp hook that checks `git log --since=<task.created_at> -- <task.files_modified>` returns ≥1 commit. If neither is provided: stamp refuses with a clear error message + suggests how to provide evidence. For backwards compatibility: warn mode (default) emits a warning; enforce mode (config `tasks.require_evidence_on_stamp = true` or `--enforce` flag) rejects the stamp with exit code 1. Human-stamped tasks and tasks with no agent/runtime attribution are exempt from the evidence requirement.

entry.summary: Install does not remove orphan skill dirs whose source skill was renamed/deleted
entry.context: On this machine: 153 user-level Claude Code skill dirs vs 95 source skill dirs in vendor/get-anything-done, leaving 58 orphans. Each orphan was once a source skill that was renamed or deleted upstream, but 'gad install --claude' only WRITES skills based on current source — it never RECONCILES against the previous manifest to prune dirs that no longer have a source.
entry.failure: Stale skills remain auto-invokable: the user-level SKILL.md still has frontmatter, still appears in skill listings, still triggers on its old keywords — even though the canonical workflow has been moved/renamed. Future agents discover and load deprecated methodology. Hardcoded blocklists in install can't keep up with skill churn.
entry.rule: Install must walk the manifest's previous file list, compare against current source, and prune anything no longer authored. The manifest is the source of truth for 'what was previously installed'; reconcile-and-prune is part of every install pass, not a separate command.

entry.summary: Stale disable-model-invocation:true frontmatter persists in user-level SKILL.md after upstream cleanup
entry.context: On this machine: 58 user-level SKILL.md files still carry 'disable-model-invocation: true' from a Cursor-suppression-script era that has since been deleted from the source tree. Current 'gad install --claude' only rewrites SKILL.md for skills whose source still exists; renamed-and-deprecated skills' user-level files retain the bad flag forever.
entry.failure: Skills are silently uninvokable. Operator wonders why a skill they 'installed' never triggers — the frontmatter flag is suppressing model-invocation but no diagnostic surfaces it. Trust in the install/skill system erodes.
entry.rule: Repair must scan ALL installed SKILL.md files (not just ones with current source), strip stale flags (disable-model-invocation, deprecated-by, etc.), and validate required-fields presence. Frontmatter hygiene is a reconcile pass over the user-level state, not a write-time concern only.

entry.summary: gad snapshot --handoff <id> errors 'Phase not found' on phase 5 despite phase 5 being active
entry.context: Worker w5 (opencode gpt-oss) claimed handoff h-2026-05-05T21-28-03-global-5 (task 05-39, phase 5 active in global). Ran 'gad snapshot --handoff h-...-global-5' to get its prompt brief. Worker stderr: 'Error: Phase not found for snapshot scope: 5'. Phase 05 IS in roadmap (status=active). Worker adapted via 'ls -R .planning/handoffs' to read handoff body directly, lost the unified prompt benefit (no auto-loaded skill bodies, no project orientation prepended).
entry.failure: Workers on legacy low-numbered phases (single-digit) get no snapshot prompt. They either fail or fall back to reading raw handoff file. Skill auto-loading + orientation lost — quality degrades for the affected work.
entry.rule: When gad snapshot resolves phase from a handoff id, normalize to string match. handoff frontmatter writes 'phase: 5' (number) — roadmap stores '05' (zero-padded string for sub-10). Convert both to int OR both to zero-padded string before comparison. Fix: lib/snapshot/scope-resolver.cjs (or wherever) — int(phase) and string(phase) both lookup roads.

entry.summary: EMFILE during gemini context scan misclassified as quota_hard_cap, parks runtime 4h
entry.context: Worker w2 ran gemini-cli on a handoff in monorepo with apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/deps/ present (Rust build artifacts, thousands of .rlib/.rmeta files). Gemini CLI's file-binary-detection walked the target tree and hit OS open-files limit: 'Failed to check if file is binary: ... EMFILE: too many open files'. Team's failure classifier read the post-crash exit and labeled it 'quota_hard_cap: billing/plan cap — operator must rotate or upgrade' with 14400000ms (4h) cooldown. Operator confirmed actual Gemini quota was 0% used. Parking spread to opencode at same time (probably same trigger — workers all share filesystem).
entry.failure: Workers idled for 4 hours on a false positive. Operator saw 'rate-limited' status and lost trust in classifier. 18 open handoffs blocked from draining for the cooldown duration.
entry.rule: Failure classifier must distinguish file-system errors (EMFILE, ENOENT, EACCES) from API quota errors. EMFILE is a 'transient local resource' error, not a quota hard cap. Cooldown should be short (seconds) or zero. Better: ALSO add a context-scan ignore list for **/target/**, **/node_modules/**, **/.next/**, **/dist/**, **/build/** in the gemini-trial.mjs wrapper so the file walker never enters those.

entry.summary: GAD_AGENT_NAME env var doesn't survive claude-code main+subagent fan-out — all subagents share parent's name
entry.context: vendor/get-anything-done/CLAUDE.md says set GAD_AGENT_NAME in env so state-log + note-add auto-fill the slug. Single-process-per-identity assumption. In claude-code v2 a single session can spawn N parallel Agent() subagents (Sonnet planner, Haiku auditor, Sonnet executor) — they all inherit parent env, all stamp as the same name. Audit trail loses ability to distinguish main vs subagent vs runtime tier. Operator caught this 2026-05-13 after I set GAD_AGENT_NAME=claude-code thinking that solved the [unknown] attribution problem.
entry.failure: Attribution false-equivalences subagents and main thread. State log + notes from parallel subagents all look identical. Cannot reconstruct who did what during a session. Trust the audit trail less.
entry.rule: Either (a) accept GAD_AGENT_NAME as runtime-identity-only and require --agent on every command that writes attribution, (b) deprecate GAD_AGENT_NAME and force explicit --agent everywhere with [unknown] as a loud failure mode, or (c) add a SessionStart-like hook that writes a dynamic value (uuid + model + role). Document the chosen path in vendor CLAUDE.md.

entry.summary: gad evolution scan refreshes .planning/.evolution-scan.json but NOT ~/.cache/gad/pressure-<id>.json — statusline stays stale after evolve
entry.context: Operator 2026-05-13: 'statusline still says to evolve now even though we just evolved'. Investigation: pressure cache at ~/.cache/gad/pressure-global.json was stuck at 2026-05-13T14:39 timestamp from earlier scan, showing score 0.89 + open_handoffs 48. Re-ran 'gad evolution scan' — .planning/.evolution-scan.json refreshed to 16:19 with current candidates, but the pressure-global.json cache stayed at 14:39. Statusline reads from ~/.cache/gad/pressure-<id>.json and shows 'evolve now'. Only 'gad snapshot' refreshes the pressure cache (running snapshot dropped score 0.89 -> 0.55 and open_handoffs 48 -> 9 immediately).
entry.failure: Operator perceives that evolution did nothing because statusline doesn't update. Erodes trust in 'gad evolution evolve' workflow. Forces operator to learn the side-channel (snapshot) to see the result of an explicit evolution.
entry.rule: Either (a) 'gad evolution scan' should call the same pressure-cache writer that 'gad snapshot' uses, (b) the statusline hook reads from .planning/.evolution-scan.json directly when fresher than the cache, or (c) 'gad evolution evolve' runs snapshot at the end as a finalizer. Pick one — operator's mental model is 'I ran evolve, statusline should reflect.'

entry.summary: Statusline ignores STATE.xml <level> and derives from XP; conflicts with operator intent that levels track evolutions
entry.context: Operator's 2026-05-09 memory feedback_evolve_equals_level_up: 'every evolution = +1 to <level value=...>. The level is the ledger entry. status line is always real time.' Operator wants levels to track evolution events, manually bumped per event. ~/.claude/hooks/gad-statusline.js readLevelSnapshot() has a comment 'Operator 2026-05-07: derive in real-time from tasks/*.json. STATE.xml <level> is no longer load-bearing — closing tasks/phases moves the bar.' Two operator decisions 2 days apart conflict: 2026-05-07 said XP-derived (in code), 2026-05-09 said event-bumped (in memory). Code never caught up to the 2026-05-09 intent. Operator 2026-05-13: 'are we really supposed to be level 4 or level 5? are we updating status and keeping it updated and how is level calculated?' — confusion is the symptom of the gap.
entry.failure: Operator can't tell what level they're at without computing two parallel ledgers (STATE.xml manual + XP-derived). Trust in statusline as 'always real time for evolutions' is broken. Currently STATE.xml=7, XP-derived statusline=3 (771/520). Off by 4 levels.
entry.rule: Resolve the conflict. Option A: change readLevelSnapshot in gad-statusline.js to read STATE.xml <level> as PRIMARY (current fallback only); use XP only for the within-level progress bar. Matches 2026-05-09 operator intent. Option B: update memory feedback_evolve_equals_level_up to point at XP discipline (skill weights, task closures = level); means dropping the 'event-bump' model. Operator picks. Filing this so the question doesn't keep recurring.

entry.summary: No reliable git attribution to distinguish team-worker commits from claude-code main-thread commits
entry.context: All commits author as operator's git identity (b2gdevs@gmail.com). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus is convention I follow for claude-code main+subagent work but workers running opencode/gemini/codex don't add it. Audit subagent dispatched 2026-05-13 to assess worker quality concluded 'zero worker commits this session' based on absence-of-co-authored-line heuristic — but at least two commits (440e9f9b dropped runtime parking, cac85a8f portfolio migration) were demonstrably worker-shipped per their handoff refs in commit messages. Audit got the wrong answer because there's no reliable signal.
entry.failure: Operator can't ask 'how are workers doing' without an audit subagent producing wrong answers. Trust in worker contribution metric is undermined. Same problem applies to attribution for evolution credit / XP / level — workers' XP earnings invisible to status surfaces.
entry.rule: When gad team worker spawns its runtime, the worker should prepend its identifier to every commit it produces. Two viable approaches: (a) commit message prefix [worker:wN] enforced at commit time by a worker-side git hook or commit-message template; (b) commit trailer Worker: wN runtime: opencode-default. Pick one; document in vendor/CLAUDE.md. After this lands, audit queries like 'workers shipped N commits this session' become a one-liner grep.
